title: Foundations: Database Architecture Data Types
summary: What database architecture data types are and why shared schemas matter.
body:
Data types for database design: schemas, indexes, queries, migrations, and replication records.

Shared data types let every system in database architecture exchange records without translation errors. This database defines the core entities — each with fields, types, a real example, and the standard it follows. Use the type-definition records to design, and the schema records to build.

title: IndexDefinition - Type Definition
summary: Field-level definition of IndexDefinition for database architecture.
body:
IndexDefinition: One index for query speed.

FIELDS:
- index_name (string): Name
- table (string): Table
- columns (array): Indexed columns
- unique (boolean): Unique?
- method (string): btree/hash/gin

EXAMPLE:
{
 "index_name": "idx_orders_customer",
 "table": "orders",
 "columns": [
  "customer_id",
  "created_at"
 ],
 "unique": false,
 "method": "btree"
}

STANDARD: Index design practice. Every record of this type should carry these fields with these meanings — that consistency is what makes data interoperable across database architecture systems.

title: QueryPlan - Type Definition
summary: Field-level definition of QueryPlan for database architecture.
body:
QueryPlan: One analyzed query plan.

FIELDS:
- query_hash (string): Hash
- sql (string): SQL text
- cost (number): Planner cost
- rows_est (number): Estimated rows
- index_used (string): Index or seq scan

EXAMPLE:
{
 "query_hash": "q9f2",
 "sql": "SELECT ... WHERE customer_id=?",
 "cost": 42.1,
 "rows_est": 120,
 "index_used": "idx_orders_customer"
}

STANDARD: EXPLAIN ANALYZE practice. Every record of this type should carry these fields with these meanings — that consistency is what makes data interoperable across database architecture systems.

title: Migration - Type Definition
summary: Field-level definition of Migration for database architecture.
body:
Migration: One schema change, versioned.

FIELDS:
- version (string): e.g. 20260601_01
- description (string): What changes
- up_sql (string): Forward SQL
- down_sql (string): Rollback SQL
- applied_at (datetime): When

EXAMPLE:
{
 "version": "20260601_01",
 "description": "add orders.status",
 "up_sql": "ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN status text",
 "down_sql": "ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN status",
 "applied_at": "2026-06-01T09:00:00Z"
}

STANDARD: Migration conventions. Every record of this type should carry these fields with these meanings — that consistency is what makes data interoperable across database architecture systems.

title: ReplicationSlot - Type Definition

title: ConstraintDefinition - Type Definition
summary: Field-level definition of ConstraintDefinition for database architecture.
body:
ConstraintDefinition: One integrity rule.

FIELDS:
- name (string): Constraint name
- table (string): Table
- kind (string): fk/unique/check
- definition (string): Rule SQL

EXAMPLE:
{
 "name": "fk_order_customer",
 "table": "orders",
 "kind": "fk",
 "definition": "FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers(id)"
}
